title: The Door Is Yours
concept: Thirty-six attorneys general, Alaska among them, settled with General Motors for $220 million over its Smart Driver program, which the complaint says logged hard braking, late-night driving and location every three seconds, sold it to Verisk and LexisNexis, who built driver ratings for insurers, some of whom used them in part to set rates. The complaint says more than 370,000 people were told they weren't enrolled while data was collected. GM admitted no violation of law, there is no claims process for drivers, and the count of Alaska drivers is not stated. The one thing the settlement fixes is the door: a driver's clear yes before collection or sharing, only what's reasonably necessary, and deletion of data kept from before January 16th, 2025. Drivers can ask GM for a copy or for deletion. A gunmetal counter named Clicky is the hero and a nickel key fob is the throughline, ending as YOUR CALL in the blank signature square.

fingerprint.palette: midnight indigo cab interior, sodium amber glow, an electric teal stream, a gunmetal counter, bone courtroom paper and magenta warning stamps
fingerprint.metaphor: a gunmetal counter that clicks every three seconds and a consent gate that finally waits for a yes, with a key fob carrying the question from ENROLLED? to YES

palette: midnight indigo cab interior, sodium amber glow, an electric teal stream, a gunmetal counter, bone courtroom paper and magenta warning stamps
divergence_note: The last five films were an overcast moss slope (11-01), a sage-and-cream chart desk (10-31), an aubergine dusk depot (10-29), a green-black sonar abyss (10-28) and a sage civic hall (10-26). This film is a night dashboard of blue-black with sodium-amber light and a teal data stream, with bone paper only in the courtroom shots and a single signal-magenta accent. Its hero is a gunmetal hand counter with eyes, and it has no slope, no desk, no depot, no sea cutaway and no hall. The signature object is a key fob that changes its engraving at every act boundary and settles YES into a blank signature square.

treatment.title: The Diary With No Signature Line
treatment.summary: Comedian's Clicky, with the Dramatist's dark fob and fair-case scene and the Explainer's pipeline, closing on the Enthusiast's door is yours.

angle.thesis: The data-to-driver-rating-to-rate pipeline is ordinary applied ML and the settlement doesn't scrap it. It rebuilds the intake valve, a driver's clear yes, which is exactly where the complaint says it broke.
angle.falsifiable_by: A record that insurers priced wholesale off these ratings (c9 says some, in part), or a decree that bans telemetry rather than fixing consent (c14 c15).
supporting_facts: c12 dealer incentives tied to enrollment
c14 to c17 every fix acts on intake
angle.counterpoint: Fixing intake pays nobody already sold: no claims process (c19), no admission (c18), no Alaska count (c22), and it's all alleged; complaint blames a glitch for c11. Honored in the TEST act as its own scene. Close on the lever drivers do have (c20).
runner_ups: enthusiast good-telematics (cut: no claim supports benefits)
